root.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Slav Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 b5

overview: After 1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.Nf3 Black defends the c4 pawn with 3...b5. White answers 4.a4 c6 5.e3 (or 5.axb5 cxb5 6.b3) and undermines the b5 pawn, usually regaining c4 with the better position. Black's plan is to hold the pawn with ...Bb7 and ...a6 or ...b4; if it fails, Black is just worse.

white_ideas.idea: Undermine b5 with a4 and axb5
Regain c4 with e3, Bxc4 or b3
Use the weak queenside to get a lasting edge

black_ideas.idea: Return the pawn if needed and play for activity

typical_structures.structure: Black queenside pawns on b5, c4 and a-file weakened, White centre pawn majority

character.notes: Tactics around a4 and b5 with Black stretched on the queenside.

gambit.notes: Black took the c4 pawn earlier and ...b5 tries to keep it, but White usually regains it by force, so not a gambit in the taxonomy sense.

soundness.notes: Considered inferior for Black; White gets an easy edge.

structure.notes: Open QGA-type with the c-file open.

approach.notes: Rare, seldom used by strong players.

character.reason: Tactical around the queenside but not a mutual attack; White usually gets a steady edge.

gambit.reason: The pawn taken on c4 is normally regained by force; Black does not give up material.

soundness.reason: White gets an easy advantage after a4.

structure.reason: QGA-type structure with the centre pawns exchanged.

level.reason: Dubious so never Beginner; little to memorise.
